title: How can a rhombus be cut and rearranged into a rectangle?
description: A rhombus has diagonals of twelve and eight centimetres. It is cut along both diagonals into four right triangles, which are joined into a rectangle as long as one diagonal and half as wide as the other. Keeko doubts this and multiplies the two whole diagonals.
teaching_notes: One idea: a rhombus rearranges into a rectangle one whole diagonal long and half the other diagonal wide. Watch for students who multiply the two whole diagonals.

source: A rhombus has diagonals 12 cm and 8 cm. Dissect it into a re
video_script.why: The child sees that cutting a rhombus along its diagonals and moving the pieces gives a rectangle, so its area is one diagonal times half the other.
video_script.substitution: Cut along the diagonals, join the right triangles in pairs, and join the two rectangles.
video_script.anchor: the book's rhombus ABCD with its diagonals crossing at O
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko multiplies the two whole diagonals, twelve times eight, which gives the rectangle round the rhombus, twice its area.
video_script.payoff_line: The area of the rhombus is forty eight square centimetres
maths_rules: rhombus ABCD: AC = 12 cm and BD = 8 cm cross at O at right angles and halve each other; AO = OC = 6 cm, BO = OD = 4 cm
four right triangles with legs 6 cm and 4 cm; two of them joined along their slanting sides make a 6 cm by 4 cm rectangle, and the other two make a second one
joined along their sides of 4 cm, the rectangles make one rectangle 12 cm by 4 cm, the length AC and half of BD (this is the book's rectangle WXYZ)
Keeko: 12 × 8 = 96, the rectangle round the rhombus, which is twice 48; the four corner triangles are 4 × 1/2 × 6 × 4 = 48 cm²
video_script.design: One rhombus all video: the diagonals cut it into four right triangles that join into a rectangle. Keeko's doubt multiplies the whole diagonals.

<bookmark mark='ask'/>What is the area of the rhombus?

narration: <bookmark mark='right'/>The two diagonals of a rhombus cross each other at a right angle.
<bookmark mark='half'/>Each diagonal cuts the other in half.
<bookmark mark='four'/>This breaks the rhombus into four right triangles that match.

beats.on_screen: Given: rhombus ABCD, diagonal AC = 12 cm, diagonal BD = 8 cm, crossing at O
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, a rhombus eigh B C D has a diagonal eigh C of twelve centimetres.
The other diagonal B D is eight centimetres.

beats.on_screen: To find: the area of the rhombus

marks.find: the thing to find is written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the area of the rhombus.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: AO = OC = 12 ÷ 2 = 6; BO = OD = 8 ÷ 2 = 4. Each right triangle has legs 6 and 4

marks.half: the point O and the halves of the diagonals are marked
marks.calc: AO = OC = 12 ÷ 2 = 6 and BO = OD = 8 ÷ 2 = 4 are written
marks.tri: the four right triangles are shown with legs 6 and 4

narration: <bookmark mark='half'/>Step one, the diagonals cut each other in half at O.
<bookmark mark='calc'/>Half of twelve is six, and half of eight is four.
<bookmark mark='tri'/>Each of the four right triangles has legs of six and four.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: turn triangle AOD over and join its slanting side to the slanting side of AOB to make a 6 by 4 rectangle; the other two triangles make a second one

marks.join: it joins AOB along the slanting side to make a rectangle 6 by 4
marks.second: the triangles COB and COD make a second 6 by 4 rectangle

narration: <bookmark mark='turn'/>Step two, turn the triangle eigh O D over.
<bookmark mark='join'/>Fit its slanting side against the slanting side of the triangle eigh O B. They make a rectangle, six by four.
<bookmark mark='second'/>The other two triangles make a second rectangle, also six by four.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: join the two rectangles along their sides of 4. Length = 6 + 6 = 12 = AC; breadth = 4 = half of BD

marks.join: the two rectangles slide together into one rectangle
marks.len: the length 12 is marked, equal to AC
marks.wid: the breadth 4 is marked, half of BD

narration: <bookmark mark='join'/>Step three, join the two rectangles along their sides of four.
<bookmark mark='len'/>The length is six plus six, which is twelve, the whole diagonal eigh C.
<bookmark mark='wid'/>The breadth is four, which is half of the diagonal B D.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: area of the rhombus = area of the rectangle = 12 × 4 = 48; check: 1/2 × 12 × 8 = 48

marks.same: an equals sign appears between the rhombus and the rectangle

narration: <bookmark mark='same'/>Step four, the rhombus has the same area as the rectangle.
<bookmark mark='calc'/>Length times breadth is twelve times four, which is forty eight.
<bookmark mark='chk'/>Check it. Half of twelve times eight is also forty eight.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The area of the rhombus is forty eight square centimetres.

narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the area is ninety six square centimetres, because twelve times eight is ninety six.
<bookmark mark='box'/>That is the area of a rectangle twelve by eight, drawn round the rhombus.
<bookmark mark='corner'/>Four corner pieces sit outside the rhombus, and together they are as big as the rhombus.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The rhombus is only half of ninety six.
